Seed cereal_rye
Rye reduced corn yields unless enough N fertilizer was applied (N immobilization).
Preferred rye seeding dates.
Prefers light loams or sands; tolerant of poor drainage.
Spring dryness window (the 30 days before planting)
Kill 7-14 days before corn planting to reduce soil water depletion.
Terminate cereal_rye
General published grain-corn nitrogen range for reference. Use the grower’s soil-test recommendation and account for relevant nutrient credits and management.
Starter fertilizer speeds early growth. Plan N source, placement and timing carefully after a small grain cover.
Corn can be planted once soil reaches 55 F; optimum dates late March through the first week of May. Conflicts with fc_pw_02 (50 F).
NC State gives 50°F as the minimum soil temperature for corn seed germination. Flag below 50°F as a germination concern. The separate 55°F row is planting gu...
Plant organic corn in the Piedmont between April 20 and May 20.
Plant after at least two days averaging above 65 F; time planting so soils are moderately dry to limit seedling disease.
Aim for 40-50 GDUs in the 4 days after planting for uniform stands.
Plant 1.5-2.5 in deep; deeper than 2.5 in can reduce stands.
Plant from June 10 to June 25 so silking avoids the July 1-20 dry period; yields vary by year.
More than 2 inches of rain in the first week after planting may hurt germination and stand establishment.
Too wet raises disease risk and reduces stands; too dry causes spotty emergence. Manual field check.
Plant field_corn
